name: two-forges
title: One Script, Two Forges
html:
One Script, Two Forges

GitHub pull request · #501 · base branch · comment GitHub REST API
gateway, at {scm} scm:pulls-getscm:mergescm:comment one kept script · one set of pins
GitLab merge request · !501 · target branch · note GitLab REST API
GitHubGitLab
The walkonce, with Claude: 20 callsnone needed
Replays5, with 0 model calls5, with 0 model calls, same script, unchanged
Promoted501, 502, 503, 505501, 502, 503, 505
Stopped by the smoke test504504
Each release56 to 61 steps, 18 to 22 s56 to 61 steps, 16 to 18 s

The only input that differs: scm, the gateway’s address.
say: And here's the part that makes it more than a neat trick. GitHub and GitLab agree on almost nothing: pull request or merge request, base branch or target branch, comment or note. The goal never names either. It says scm:merge, scm:comment, scm:pulls-get. So does the kept script. A small gateway in front of each forge serves those same forms on top of that forge's own API. The only thing that differs between a GitHub release and a GitLab release is one input: the gateway's address. The script walked once on GitHub replayed five merge requests on GitLab, unchanged, with no model. Four promoted. 504 stopped, on both, as it should.

deck:ref.label: scm:
deck:ref.title: scm: one set of typed relations, two forges
deck:ref.summary: scm:merge, scm:comment, scm:close and the rest: relation names defined by meaning, not by one server's endpoints. GitHub and GitLab both answer to them, so a kept script runs on either.

deck:ref.name: gateway
deck:ref.label: GATEWAY
deck:ref.title: The gateway: our controls in front of theirs
deck:ref.summary: A small server, on a laptop, in front of an API we don't control (GitHub, a local GitLab). YAML connectors map each act onto the native call and say when it is offered; the gateway answers in HEART.

deck:ref.name: layered-system
deck:ref.label: LAYERED
deck:ref.title: Layered system (§5.1.6)
deck:ref.summary: Each component sees only the next layer; intermediaries can cache and enforce policy. A gateway in front of GitHub is this.
deck:ref.quote: “In order to further improve behavior for Internet-scale requirements, we add layered system constraints (Figure 5-7). As described in Section 3.4.2, the layered system style allows an architecture to be composed of hierarchical layers by constraining component behavior such that each component cannot "see" beyond the immediate layer with which they are interacting. By restricting knowledge of the system to a single layer, we place a bound on the overall system complexity and promote substrate independence. Layers can be used to encapsulate legacy services and to protect new services from legacy clients, simplifying components by moving infrequently used functionality to a shared intermediary. Intermediaries can also be used to improve system scalability by enabling load balancing of services across multiple networks and processors.”
deck:ref.cite: Roy T. Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures, §5.1.6
